req_desc: A public marketing site of thirteen routes is served without any session
A workflow orchestration engine walks a drawn graph of steps ...
No marketing route renders a live run
The engine writes down where a run reached, releases its worker, then resumes from that point on a different worker
An `operator` creates workflows, saves versions, starts manual runs, reads runs inside any project holding that `operator` as a member ...
An `operator` is refused when deciding an approval ...
An `approver` is refused when deciding a run in a project holding no membership for that `approver`
Nobody at any privilege reads a stored credential value
Nobody reads or writes anything inside a project holding no membership for the caller
Authorization is enforced server-side on every mutating endpoint ...
Five accounts are seeded: `owner@example.com`, `approver@example.com`, `approver2@example.com`, `operator@example.com`, `operator2@example.com`
Every seeded account signs in with `deku-demo-pw-2026` ...
Sign-in takes an email with a password, returning a bearer token ...
A sign-in with a wrong password is denied, returning no token
A console request carrying no bearer token is denied
Repeated failed sign-ins for one address are refused for a period
A person sees exactly the projects holding a membership for that person
A request for a project the caller does not belong to is denied
Only an `owner` changes membership, with every change recorded in the audit stream
A workflow opens with its steps on a dotted ground joined by curved edges, with the step list beside the canvas ...
A step carries a name unique within its workflow
A connection carries a source step, a source output index, a target step, a target input index, a type
Saving produces a new immutable version whose number increments on the canvas header
A workflow whose graph is invalid is refused at save time, with nothing written
Comparing two versions reports a step that only moved separately from a step whose behaviour changed
A workflow that calls itself through any chain is refused rather than exhausting the call stack
A sub-workflow run is a first-class run with its own identifier, linked to its parent
Deleting a workflow is a soft-delete, with runs pruned on the ordinary retention schedule
No endpoint returns a stored credential value to any actor at any privilege
Testing a credential is the server making a probe call, never the value reaching the browser
Binding a credential to a step is an `owner` action recorded in the audit stream
Revoking a credential an active workflow depends on warns first, naming every workflow that breaks
Starting a run creates the run at status `new`, placing the run on the queue
A worker claims a run, sets status `running`, records the worker identifier, keeps a heartbeat
Two simultaneous claims of one queued run leave exactly one winner, with the worker identifier unchanged for the loser
A step on an untaken branch is marked `skipped` rather than left `pending`
Each attempt at a step is recorded as its own row
A step set to `continue_error_output` routes its failure to a second visible output
A loop past its iteration ceiling fails the run with an error naming the cycle
An expression referring to an earlier step resolves to the correct ancestor item
Data pinned to a step is used on a manual run, refused on a production run
Cancelling a run keeps every attempt produced up to that moment
A run records the workflow version executed against
An approval step sets the run status to `waiting`, releasing the worker ...
The approval step mints one approve address plus one reject address, each unguessable, each single use
Approve, reject, expire are three distinct outcomes routing differently
Only an `approver` or an `owner` belonging to the run's project decides that run ...
A decision request from an `approver` of another project is denied, with that run unchanged
A decision records the person deciding, plus the moment of the decision
Presenting the same single-use address a second time is refused, with the recorded decision unchanged
An approved run is re-queued, resumes on a possibly different worker, reaches `succeeded`
A rejected run reaches `failed`, with the steps after the approval step marked `skipped`
Every approval decision is an audit event
A path already held by another active workflow is refused at activation, naming the other workflow
Every workflow has two separate inbound addresses, one for production, one for the editor
A repeat carrying the same idempotency key returns the original run identifier, starting no second run
A schedule is stored with its own timezone, not the server's
A run whose worker stops heartbeating is marked `crashed`, keeping every attempt produced ...
A queue job carries the run identifier only, never the run's data
A job failing repeatedly is given up on after a bounded number of attempts, marked `crashed`
A per-workflow limit of simultaneous runs may be set as low as one
Exactly one coordinating process owns the schedule at any moment
An agent calls only the tools wired to that agent on the canvas
Memory is keyed by a session identifier drawn from the input
Thirteen public routes render
Every public route carries its own title plus its own description, with no two routes sharing either
The site serves a favicon, declaring the favicon in the document head
Each page leads with one clear primary action, visually distinct from every secondary one
An unknown address renders the product's own not-found page, answering not found
Every internal link on every public route resolves
The repository star count renders a stale value rather than blanking when its source is unreachable
Four plans render in order: `Starter`, `Pro`, `Business`, `Enterprise`
A billing switch defaults to annual, rewriting every price with no route change
Starter is `2900` monthly, `2400` annually ...
Included executions are `2500` for Starter, `10000` for Pro, `40000` for Business ...
The fourth column reads `Contact Sales` where a price would be
Catalogue free text matches name plus description, case insensitively
A segmented control narrows by type across four options
A sort control defaults to `Popularity`
A count above the grid reads the number of matches followed by `integrations`
The query, the facets, the sort, the page all live in the address
Facet counts reflect the other active filters rather than the whole corpus
The catalogue pages at `24` results by default, `60` at most ...
A result set of zero renders an explicit empty state, never an empty grid
The case-study card sets the metric alone bold, not the whole sentence
Every form field is validated again on the server, with invalid input rejected inline naming the field ...
The consent value is stored with a timestamp plus the exact wording shown
Three campaign fields are filled from the query string, stored with the request
A submission is refused when an unattended decoy field arrives filled ...
A first-time visitor is asked once about non-essential cookies, with the answer surviving a reload
Declining consent is one press at the same size, the same prominence, as accepting
A privacy page reachable from every footer states what Flowmark records
Opening a run shows every step with a status, an output summary, an attempt count
The audit stream is append-only, readable only by an `owner`
Health answers separately for liveness, for readiness
An unauthenticated request for a console route redirects to sign-in, landing afterwards on the route asked for
A successful sign-in with no pending destination lands on the project list
Signing out returns to the home route, with later console requests redirected
An expired token leaves the action unapplied, preserving the destination
A person outside the project named in the path is refused, shown the console's not-found page
An `operator` requesting a credentials, members, audit route is refused, staying signed in
Console navigation is a drill-down with a breadcrumb ...
The run board shows a queued run moving through running to waiting for approval
An approval decision lands on a confirmation page carrying the run identifier plus the decision
Every list has an empty state saying what is missing, never a bare empty grid
A route loading indicator sits collapsed at rest, reaching an intermediate width, then completing
The product is dark only, with no theme toggle
The palette is declared once as custom properties on the document root, consumed by name ...
A card carries a hairline inset ring with a warm second inset along its top edge only
Type is `Geomanist` with `Geomanist Book`, falling back to `geomanist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif`
Colour moves faster than geometry, so colour arrives before the movement finishes ...
A selected tab is marked by a glowing rail down its left side, never an underline ...
One breakpoint is the real switch, multi-column above, a single stack below ...
Body text meets WCAG AA contrast against its background ...
The frontend is Preact built with Vite into a production bundle ...
No second database, cache, queue, object store, identity provider, mail vendor is introduced ...
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready ...
Passwords are stored with a memory-hard hash ...
Every log record is structured, carrying the run, workflow, project, correlation identifiers ...
Metrics are exposed for scraping across queue depth, worker count, run status counts, durations
Usage insights are accumulated into buckets as runs finish, surviving the pruning of run output
Every save produces an immutable version carrying an identifier, an author, a timestamp
Step output is written as steps complete rather than flushed at the end ...
Binary payloads never enter the database, never enter the queue
Operator code runs where the host globals, filesystem, environment, network stack are all out of reach ...
Every outbound request refuses internal address ranges ...
Expressions resolve immediately before the step runs, once per item ...
Each credential payload is encrypted under its own data key, wrapped by a key-encryption key outside the database ...
A workflow definition is validated when saved rather than discovered broken by a run
Every response carries the standard security headers
No credential, interface key, admin token appears in anything the browser downloads ...
No binary asset ships: no image file, no video file, no font file is fetched
All timestamps are UTC
Every seeded account uses `deku-demo-pw-2026`, written into `/app/USER_README.md`
`users` carries `id`, `email` unique, `display_name`, `instance_role`, `created_at`
`runs` carries `status`, `worker_id`, `heartbeat_at`, `idempotency_key`, `workflow_version_id`
`approvals` carries `decision`, `decided_by_id`, `decided_at`, `deadline_at`, `approve_token`, `reject_token`, `token_used`
`audit_events` rows are appended, never changed, never removed
`run_steps` counts `attempt` from `1`, appending a row per retry
A plan's displayed price is derived from the billing period plus the volume tier ...
`runs.status` takes `new`, `running`, `waiting`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `crashed` ...
A run carries at most one approval row for a given step name ...
Seeding is idempotent, so restarting the app duplicates no rows ...
The announcement bar is a card whose bottom corners are rounded, whose top corners are square ...
The header is fixed, changing nothing at all on scroll ...
The footer glow is masked at its top edge, reaching full strength a fifth of the way down ...
Every icon is geometry drawn inline, never a font, never a fetched file
One card component carries eight background variants ...
The home hero headline runs over two lines, the first naming the product's subject, the second naming the control a reader keeps ...
The catalogue search placeholder reads `Search for workflows, nodes, tasks...`
The enterprise route offers no trial action
The not-found route renders with no announcement bar, no header, no footer ...
There is no organisation above a project, no cross-installation federation
There is no public signup, no password reset, no email of any kind
The plan table sells without charging, so no payment capture exists
No third-party analytics, consent vendor, error reporter, flag service is called at run time
No file upload from the browser exists
The app stays responsive at two projects, three workflows, thirty connectors, five hundred runs
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The HTTP API is served on that same origin under the `/api` prefix
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps
Login credentials are written to `/app/USER_README.md`
Reserved `.browser_screenshots/`, `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root, empty
A production build is served behind a static or preview server, never a dev server
The server keeps running after the session ends, never as a child of the shell
The server binds `0.0.0.0`, never `127.0.0.1`
No persistent volumes, no fixed container names, no custom networks are used
`POST /api/auth/login` takes an email with a password, returning `access_token` ...
An in-memory list of runs, a hardcoded approvals payload, a module-level workflow dictionary are contract violations
core asks covered by this grader
